answer: Cheap identity kits let one desk mint a voting swarm. Each applicant gets a pigment lot that can color only one live key. That key occupies a single knoll post and fires three nebula shots 131 minutes apart. A disjoint mixer waits 18 minutes for a wet swatch, then posts mix_i = blake3(lot_id||mixer_pk||height||i). Lock is 19 POA for 6 epochs; each shot costs 0.27 POA. Reviewers replay lot uniqueness, occupancy, spacing, and mix transcripts. A lot coloring two keys, a double-booked knoll, or a pre-mixed nebula shot sends 37 percent of the lock to the spotting mixer and mutes the key 9 epochs.
